name: player
description: A lightweight 2.5D character player for the web, with lip sync and webcam face tracking.
readmeExcerpt:
A lightweight 2.5D character player for the web, with lip sync and webcam face tracking. A few lines of code put a character in a page, a stream overlay or an app.
Comes with 21 featured characters in different styles, ready to use.

English · 中文 · 日本語 · Tiếng Việt

- WebGL2, no dependencies, about 30 KB gzipped for the core - Lip sync (microphone, audio, video) and webcam face tracking (MediaPipe), both in the browser, imported only when you need them - Plays LivLiv, VRM and PNGTuber characters through the same API - 21 featured characters in [`characters/`](characters/), ready to use ## Try it - **Online**: the examples run on [livliv-dev.github.io/player](https://livliv-dev.github.io/player/). - **Here**: `npm install && npm run build`, serve this folder with any static server and open `/example/demo.html` (expressions, actions, microphone, camera; `?model=../characters//` picks another character). `/example/png.html` and `/example/vrm.html` show a PNGTuber and a VRM. - **On livliv.ai**: each character's page there plays it with the same renderer. Start at [livliv.ai/discover](https://livliv.ai/discover). ## Project LivLiv We want the art of creating characters to belong to everyone. We're open-sourcing our AI tools for character creation, the player and its playback protocol, and a stage where your characters can meet an audience. Come say hello on [Discord](https://discord.gg/ac5qF36T2H) and follow us on [X (Twitter)](https://x.com/livliv_ai). ## Use it in your page ```sh npm install @livliv-dev/player ``` ```js import { Player } from '@livliv-dev/player' const player = new Player(document.querySelector('canvas')) await player.load('characters/k01/') // a folder with model.json and textures/, or a .livliv file player.setExpression('smile') // ids are in player.expressions player.act('nod') player.params.mouthOpen = 0.6 // 0..1 ``` Lip sync and face tracking: ```js import { createSpeech } from '@livliv-dev/player/voice' import { startFaceTracking } from '@livliv-dev/player/tracking' // needs @mediapipe/tasks-vision const speech = createSpeech(player) button.onclick = () => { speech.unlock(); speech.say('/reply.mp3') } await startFaceTracking(player) ``` A VRM or a PNGTuber, on the same API: ```js import { BodyPlayer } from '@livliv-dev/player/body' import { VrmBody } from '@livliv-dev/player/vrm' // needs three and @pixiv/three-vrm import { PngBody } from '@livliv-dev/player/png' const vrm = new BodyPlayer(canvasA, new VrmBody()) await vrm.load('/avatars/me.vrm') const png = new BodyPlayer(canvasB, new PngBody()) await png.load({ closed: 'me-closed.png', open: 'me-open.png' }) ``` The whole API is in [API.md](API.md): options, params, expressions and actions, drivers, VRM and PNGTuber characters, the limits on untrusted files, the model package and the format version. The LivLiv package format (`.livliv`, `model.json` v4) is in [FORMAT.md](FORMAT.md), with a JSON Schema in [`schema/`](schema/); packages exported before v4 are described in [FORMAT-v3.md](FORMAT-v3.md) and still play. > The npm package is the player alone. The featured characters are in this repository's [`characters/`](characters/): copy > the ones you use next to your page, with their licence. ## Featured characters `characters/` holds 21 characters, ready to `load()`. They carry a small LivLiv mark in the bottom-right corner, which the player draws. They are **not** covered by the Apache License. Most were made by LivLiv: use those free for personal, non-commercial projects with credit ("Characters: LivLiv (livliv.ai)"); don't sell them, use them commercially or train AI models on them. Nana is LivLiv's mascot. The terms are in [characters/LICENSE.md](characters/LICENSE.md). Kujira, Kujira Q and Pen come from other people's work: that licence and that credit don't cover them. Their sources, credits and terms are in [characters/CREDITS.md](characters/CREDITS.md). Each also has a `cover.webp` (512 x 768, about 50 KB), its first frame without the mark. `player.load(source, { poster })` shows it on the canvas until the first frame. To have it before any script has run, put it under the canvas with `object-fit: contain` and fade the character in over it, as [example/loading.js](example/loading.js) does. | id | name | id | name | id | name | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | `k01` | Sena | `d01` | Yui | `v01` | Aster | | `k02` | Elio | `d02` | Leo | `v03` | Mira | | `char06` | Aoi | `d03` | Nana | `v04` | Kai | | `char07` | Sora | `d03ft` | Nana (refined) | `v05` | Lilith | | `s01` | Hana | `p01` | Kujira | `v06` | Usa | | `q02` | Mochi | `p02` | Kujira Q | `v07` | Stella | | `q03` | Kotaro | `p03` | Pen | `w01` | Max | ## Characters of your own You can bring in a PNGTuber's pictures, or a VRM (drawn with three.js); or make a character of your own from one picture on [livliv.ai](https://livliv.ai). - **A PNGTuber**: two pictures (mouth closed, mouth open), and two more with the eyes closed if you have them. - **A VRM**: from VRoid Studio or any tool that exports VRM 0.x or 1.0. - **A LivLiv model**: make one from a picture on [livliv.ai](https://livliv.ai), then download its model package from the character's page (**Model package**): a `.livliv` file. Pass it to `load()` as it is (a URL, or the `File` someone picked), or unzipped as a folder. Packages on the free plan carry the LivLiv mark, and the player draws it. ## About the player and the characters LivLiv Player and the `.livliv` format are LivLiv's own work. They use no Live2D software or Cubism SDK and do not read `.moc3` or `.cmo3` files. "Live2D" is a trademark of Live2D Inc.; LivLiv is not affiliated with it. Making a character on livliv.ai uses AI. The player itself only plays: it calls no AI service and reads only the files you point it at. Face tracking runs Google's MediaPipe in the browser, and camera images stay on the device; API.md has the networking details. The featured characters in this repository were made on LivLiv too, also with AI; Kujira, Kujira Q and Pen adapt other people's characters ([credits](characters/CREDITS.md)). Refined Nana (`d03ft`) also has swinging parts and head-turn keyforms added with LivLiv's own tools. A package's `meta.author` and `meta.license` record who made it and on what terms: keep them and follow them. When you show a character made with LivLiv in public, say that AI was used to make it, and don't present it as hand-drawn or hand-rigged. ## Embed without code ```html ``` The same `/live/` page has a transparent background and works as an OBS Browser Source.\ (Powered by [https://livliv.ai](https://livliv.ai)) ## Develop ```sh git clone https://github.com/livliv-dev/player cd player npm install npm run check # types npm run build # dist/: index.js, tracking.js, voice.js, body.js, png.js, vrm.js (ES modules), chunks/ and types/ npm test # unit and fuzz tests (Node 22.18 or newer, no browser) npm run test:browser # every featured character drawn in headless Chromium; once: npx playwright-core install chromium-headless-shell npm run test:engines # a sample on Firefox and WebKit, where WebGL2 starts (a GPU or a software GL); once: npx playwright-core install firefox webkit ``` `src/runtime/` is the renderer and motion code livliv.ai runs; this repository is published from it. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). Security reports: [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). ## Browser support WebGL2 and ES2023: Chrome / Edge 97+, Firefox 104+, Safari 15.4+. Tested on current desktop browsers, not yet on phones. ## License The code is under the [Apache License 2.0](LICENSE) (see also [NOTICE](NOTICE)). The featured characters have their own licence, [characters/LICENSE.md](characters/LICENSE.md). Neither licence covers the LivLiv name and logos. ## Thanks Thanks to 上善无形, ZipZipPipe and 贱兔死顺盖, whose characters Kujira, Kujira Q and Pen are based on: see [characters/CREDITS.md](characters/CREDITS.md).

releases.name: LivLiv Player 0.3.0
releases.body:
The first version of LivLiv Player on npm. The interface settled first, so a page written for 0.2 needs a few changes. Format 4 is unchanged.

## What to change from 0.2

| 0.2 | 0.3 |
|---|---|
| `import ... from '@livliv/player'` and its subpaths | `'@livliv-dev/player'`, the package's name on npm. |
| `player.act('away')` | `player.setAway(true)` and `setAway(false)`. `act('away')` now throws: it was a switch among one-off moves. |
| `player.puppet` | No longer in the types. `player.poke()` and `player.canvasToModel()` are what pages used it for. The field still exists and can change in any version. |
| `player.load(a); player.load(b)` played `a`, then `b` | The new load replaces the one running, which rejects with an `AbortError`. If you catch errors, let this one through: `if (e.name === 'AbortError') return`. |
| `dispose()` on a load running rejected with an `Error` | It rejects with an `AbortError`, as `load()` on a disposed player does. |
| Errors told apart by their message | `e.code`, on a `LivLivError`. The messages can change. |

## Install

```sh
npm install @livliv-dev/player
```

## Character sources and terms, corrected

- **Kujira and Kujira Q** are under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, not the LivLiv Featured Characters License. They are based on the community "whale girl" (鲸鱼娘): original character 溟月 by 上善无形, maid design by ZipZipPipe. Credit: "Kujira: 上善无形, ZipZipPipe (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0); model by LivLiv".

releases.name: LivLiv Player 0.2.0
releases.body:
The first public release of LivLiv Player: a lightweight 2.5D character player for the web, with lip sync and webcam face tracking. It comes with 21 featured characters, ready to use.

## What's in it

- **`Player`** plays a LivLiv model (a `.livliv` file, or its folder) on a `<canvas>` with WebGL2: layered 2D art that turns its head with depth. No dependencies; about 34 KB gzipped for the core, idle motion included.
- **Idle motion**: breathing, blinking, and following the pointer with the eyes and head. `setExpression()`, `act()` (`nod`, `shake`, `tilt`, `hop`, `shy`, `away`), `lookAt()` and `blink()` on top.
- **Lip sync** (`@livliv-dev/player/voice`): from the microphone, a `MediaStream`, an `<audio>` or `<video>` element, or clips queued with `speech.say()`.
- **Face tracking** (`@livliv-dev/player/tracking`): webcam tracking with MediaPipe, in the browser. Camera images stay on the device; API.md has the networking details.
- **VRM and PNGTuber characters** (`@livliv-dev/player/body`, `/vrm`, `/png`): the same API, lip sync and face tracking included. VRM 0.x and 1.0 need `three` and `@pixiv/three-vrm`, both optional.

readmeHtml:
A lightweight 2.5D character player for the web, with lip sync and webcam face tracking. A few lines of code put a character in a page, a stream overlay or an app.
Comes with 21 featured characters in different styles, ready to use.

English · 中文 · 日本語 · Tiếng Việt

  • WebGL2, no dependencies, about 30 KB gzipped for the core
  • Lip sync (microphone, audio, video) and webcam face tracking (MediaPipe), both in the browser, imported only when you need them
  • Plays LivLiv, VRM and PNGTuber characters through the same API
  • 21 featured characters in characters/, ready to use

Try it

  • Online: the examples run on livliv-dev.github.io/player.
  • Here: npm install && npm run build, serve this folder with any static server and open /example/demo.html (expressions, actions, microphone, camera; ?model=../characters/<id>/ picks another character). /example/png.html and /example/vrm.html show a PNGTuber and a VRM.
  • On livliv.ai: each character's page there plays it with the same renderer. Start at livliv.ai/discover.

Project LivLiv

We want the art of creating characters to belong to everyone.

We're open-sourcing our AI tools for character creation, the player and its playback protocol, and a stage where your characters can meet an audience.

Come say hello on Discord and follow us on X (Twitter).

Use it in your page

npm install @livliv-dev/player
import { Player } from '@livliv-dev/player'

const player = new Player(document.querySelector('canvas'))
await player.load('characters/k01/')   // a folder with model.json and textures/, or a .livliv file

player.setExpression('smile')          // ids are in player.expressions
player.act('nod')
player.params.mouthOpen = 0.6          // 0..1

Lip sync and face tracking:

import { createSpeech } from '@livliv-dev/player/voice'
import { startFaceTracking } from '@livliv-dev/player/tracking'   // needs @mediapipe/tasks-vision

const speech = createSpeech(player)
button.onclick = () => { speech.unlock(); speech.say('/reply.mp3') }

await startFaceTracking(player)

A VRM or a PNGTuber, on the same API:

import { BodyPlayer } from '@livliv-dev/player/body'
import { VrmBody } from '@livliv-dev/player/vrm'    // needs three and @pixiv/three-vrm
import { PngBody } from '@livliv-dev/player/png'

const vrm = new BodyPlayer(canvasA, new VrmBody())
await vrm.load('/avatars/me.vrm')
const png = new BodyPlayer(canvasB, new PngBody())
await png.load({ closed: 'me-closed.png', open: 'me-open.png' })

The whole API is in API.md: options, params, expressions and actions, drivers, VRM and PNGTuber characters, the limits on untrusted files, the model package and the format version. The LivLiv package format (.livliv, model.json v4) is in FORMAT.md, with a JSON Schema in schema/; packages exported before v4 are described in FORMAT-v3.md and still play.

The npm package is the player alone. The featured characters are in this repository's characters/: copy the ones you use next to your page, with their licence.

Featured characters

characters/ holds 21 characters, ready to load(). They carry a small LivLiv mark in the bottom-right corner, which the player draws. They are not covered by the Apache License. Most were made by LivLiv: use those free for personal, non-commercial projects with credit ("Characters: LivLiv (livliv.ai)"); don't sell them, use them commercially or train AI models on them. Nana is LivLiv's mascot. The terms are in characters/LICENSE.md.

Kujira, Kujira Q and Pen come from other people's work: that licence and that credit don't cover them. Their sources, credits and terms are in characters/CREDITS.md.

Each also has a cover.webp (512 x 768, about 50 KB), its first frame without the mark. player.load(source, { poster }) shows it on the canvas until the first frame. To have it before any script has run, put it under the canvas with object-fit: contain and fade the character in over it, as example/loading.js does.

k02 Elio d02 Leo v03 Mira

char07 Sora d03ft Nana (refined) v05 Lilith

q03 Kotaro p03 Pen w01 Max

Characters of your own

You can bring in a PNGTuber's pictures, or a VRM (drawn with three.js); or make a character of your own from one picture on livliv.ai.

  • A PNGTuber: two pictures (mouth closed, mouth open), and two more with the eyes closed if you have them.
  • A VRM: from VRoid Studio or any tool that exports VRM 0.x or 1.0.
  • A LivLiv model: make one from a picture on livliv.ai, then download its model package from the character's page (Model package): a .livliv file. Pass it to load() as it is (a URL, or the File someone picked), or unzipped as a folder. Packages on the free plan carry the LivLiv mark, and the player draws it.

About the player and the characters

LivLiv Player and the .livliv format are LivLiv's own work. They use no Live2D software or Cubism SDK and do not read .moc3 or .cmo3 files. "Live2D" is a trademark of Live2D Inc.; LivLiv is not affiliated with it.

Making a character on livliv.ai uses AI. The player itself only plays: it calls no AI service and reads only the files you point it at. Face tracking runs Google's MediaPipe in the browser, and camera images stay on the device; API.md has the networking details.

The featured characters in this repository were made on LivLiv too, also with AI; Kujira, Kujira Q and Pen adapt other people's characters (credits). Refined Nana (d03ft) also has swinging parts and head-turn keyforms added with LivLiv's own tools.

A package's meta.author and meta.license record who made it and on what terms: keep them and follow them. When you show a character made with LivLiv in public, say that AI was used to make it, and don't present it as hand-drawn or hand-rigged.

Embed without code

<iframe src="https://livliv.ai/live/k01" width="480" height="640" allow="camera; microphone"
  style="border:0;background:transparent"></iframe>

The same /live/<id> page has a transparent background and works as an OBS Browser Source.
(Powered by https://livliv.ai)

Develop

git clone https://github.com/livliv-dev/player
cd player
npm install
npm run check          # types
npm run build          # dist/: index.js, tracking.js, voice.js, body.js, png.js, vrm.js (ES modules), chunks/ and types/
npm test               # unit and fuzz tests (Node 22.18 or newer, no browser)
npm run test:browser   # every featured character drawn in headless Chromium; once: npx playwright-core install chromium-headless-shell
npm run test:engines   # a sample on Firefox and WebKit, where WebGL2 starts (a GPU or a software GL); once: npx playwright-core install firefox webkit

src/runtime/ is the renderer and motion code livliv.ai runs; this repository is published from it. See CONTRIBUTING.md. Security reports: SECURITY.md.

Browser support

WebGL2 and ES2023: Chrome / Edge 97+, Firefox 104+, Safari 15.4+. Tested on current desktop browsers, not yet on phones.

License

The code is under the Apache License 2.0 (see also NOTICE). The featured characters have their own licence, characters/LICENSE.md. Neither licence covers the LivLiv name and logos.

Thanks

Thanks to 上善无形, ZipZipPipe and 贱兔死顺盖, whose characters Kujira, Kujira Q and Pen are based on: see characters/CREDITS.md.

aiSummary.oneLiner: Customizable, lightweight HTML5 video player component.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: This project provides a modern HTML5 video player focused on performance and customizability. It offers a clean default UI while allowing extensive styling via CSS variables. The player handles common media events and provides a simplified API for playback control. It is built without heavy dependencies to ensure fast load times. The architecture supports plugins for adding features like analytics or ads.
keyFeatures: Customizable UI: allows complete restyling of controls using CSS variables.
Plugin system: supports extending functionality with modular JavaScript plugins.
Event handling: normalizes HTML5 media events into a consistent API.
Keyboard accessibility: includes built-in support for standard keyboard shortcuts.
Responsive design: adapts automatically to different screen sizes and orientations.

useCases.title: Custom Media Platforms
useCases.description: Build branded video experiences without relying on generic iframes.

useCases.title: Lightweight Embedding
useCases.description: Embed videos on landing pages with minimal impact on load times.

useCases.title: Interactive Video
useCases.description: Extend the player with custom overlays or interactive elements.

useCases.title: Accessible Playback
useCases.description: Ensure video content is navigable via keyboard and screen readers.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Frontend developers building custom video experiences on the web. It is ideal for projects that require a player lighter and more flexible than standard libraries.
